subject: Dedicated capacity structure, requested credits & commit path
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@novamed.io>
To: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@novamed.io
Date: Sun, 25 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated sizing + ask on credits for competitive match

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile on long-context reranks. We're preparing a business case for internal procurement and legal, and two items came up that I wanted to surface early:

1) Dedicated sizing: our inference workload is spiky around end-of-month batch scoring (we expect 50–70k concurrent prompt tokens during peaks). We'd like a proposed GPU pool topology and an estimate for sustained throughput at 4s p99 and at 2s p95 for 16k context.

2) Commercial ask: We're entertaining a parallel proposal from a regional provider who is offering a 12‑month reserved commit with a 20% credit back in year 1 if we exceed baseline usage. To stay competitive, can Redwood provide a credits/discount path or a limited promotion tied to a 12–18 month committed pool? We're not asking for a blanket concession — more like a structured credit if we hit agreed throughput thresholds.

I've attached a brief requirements spreadsheet and included legal on cc so we can align on timing. We're targeting a procurement decision by Aug 5.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of ML Platforms
NovaMed

Attachments: NovaMed_requirements_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing + ask on credits for competitive match

Hi Elena — thanks for the clarity and the sheet. Quick response: we can model a pool that meets the p99/p95 objectives but the exact GPU mix depends on your preferred latency/cost tradeoff. I'll loop in Marissa and Aditya to give a written sizing + a commercial path.

Next steps as I see them:
- Redwood to send a technical proposal (GPU topology + throughput targets) by Wed 7/28.
- Commercial proposal with a conditional credit structure by Fri 7/30 so you have time for procurement review.

If that timeline works I'll put the deliverables in a short doc and share a link.

Thanks — Irene
Irene Choi
Sr. Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal draft (internal) — NovaMed sizing + credit construct

Team — draft for internal review before we send to Elena:

Technical suggestion (short):
- Baseline pool: 8x A100-80GB equiv (continuous) + 4x A100 burst nodes for month-end windows. Estimated sustained throughput: ~1.1M tokens/min at 4s p99 for 16k context, burst to 1.8M tokens/min at 2s p95 with autoscale.

Commercial proposal (conditional credit):
- 12‑month reserved commit at $X/month (confidential).
- Conditional throughput credit: if measured monthly throughput > 115% of committed baseline for any two months in a quarter -> 15% credit applied to following month invoice (credit capped at 25% of monthly commit).
- One-time onboarding credit of $10k if contract signed before Aug 10.

Requesting approvals: Vivek — need okay on the conditional credit structure and cap. Aditya — confirm we can instrument the throughput SLA and measure for credit triggers (metrics + auditability).

I'll attach the consumer-facing proposal after we get the greenlight.

-Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering

Attachment: redwood_dedicated_proposal_20270801.pdf (internal draft)

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal draft (internal) — NovaMed sizing + credit construct

Thanks for the clear draft. Approve the approach with two caveats:
1) Cap the cumulative credits at 3 months equivalent of committed monthly fee over the 12‑month term (protects economics).
2) Add a 30‑day lookback window for disputed measurements and require NovaMed to grant view-only access to their usage dashboard for auditing.

If legal signs off on those points I'm comfortable for Sales to present. Also, defer onboarding credit to discretionary exec approval — I'd like a short memo (one paragraph) summarizing strategic rationale (logo, referenceable case, competitive displacement) if we lean on the $10k onboarding concession.

-Vivek
Head of Sales Operations

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal draft (internal) — NovaMed sizing + credit construct

Confirming instrumentation: we can measure committed baseline vs observed throughput using token-level telemetry tied to the committed pool ID. For auditability: we'll provide daily aggregates and a monthly attestation CSV. The lookback window is implementable — we'll keep raw traces for 90 days.

On the onboarding credit: happy to draft the one-paragraph exec memo. Proposed rationale: NovaMed is a top-10 strategic target in life sciences (referenceable pilot with multi-team buy-in). The $10k onboarding credit is offset by ~2 months of committed margin in Yr1 but materially increases likelihood of a win in a competitive bake-off.

I'll attach a suggested commit_sheet for the commercial terms (commit_sheet_novamed.xlsx) for Irene to review before external send.

-Aditya
Sr. Solutions Architect
